knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly matches basic hypothesis-test settings to designs and models?
knowledge_checks.body: Select one-sample / two-sample / paired and Normal vs discrete.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Match design (one-sample, two-sample, paired) and model (Normal, binomial, Poisson). Permutation tests are a different approach; equal n does not erase pairing.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: One-sample / two-sample / paired designs; Normal and binomial/Poisson basic tests.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using permutation as the basic parametric test, or mishandling paired vs independent designs.

choices.label: One-sample tests a single population parameter; two-sample compares independent groups; paired uses matched differences. Basic procedures include Normal mean tests and binomial/Poisson tests under CMP conditions.
Paired data should be analysed with the independent two-sample test whenever n₁ = n₂.
Permutation reshuffling of labels is the basic parametric test for Normal means in this learning objective.
Binomial and Poisson data never use basic tests; only continuous Normal means appear.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly names the basic test family for each setting and keeps permutation distinct?
knowledge_checks.body: Match settings to basic tests; refuse permutation-as-basic.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Basic tests follow the sampling model and design. Permutation is separate. Scrambling designs (paired vs independent, one-sample vs two-sample) produces the wrong procedure.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: z-test for one Normal mean (σ known); two-sample proportion test; paired test on differences; permutation ≠ basic parametric.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Calling a permutation shuffle the basic-test requirement, or mismatching design to procedure.

choices.label: (a) one Normal mean with σ known → one-sample Normal/z-test; (b) two independent binomial proportions → two-sample proportion test with Normal approximation; (c) paired Normal differences → paired test on differences. Permutation tests are a different approach, not a substitute for these basic parametric tests.
(a) chi-square GOF; (b) paired t on raw unpaired columns; (c) independent two-sample z on matched pairs.
All three settings are handled by shuffling treatment labels under a permutation null; parametric Normal/binomial tests are optional flavour.
(a) two-sample z for one mean; (b) one-sample Poisson test for two proportions; (c) binomial test for paired Normal differences.
